summary: Console: Latency dashboard missing eu-west region breakdown (region filter + charts)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports the Console > Observability > Latency dashboard does not show eu-west as a selectable region, and charts appear to be missing eu-west series (no breakdown / only us-east/us-west).
- Customer expectation: ability to view p50/p95 latency and error rate by region, including eu-west, for the last 24h/7d.

Impact
- Customer cannot self-serve latency reporting for eu-west via Console (blocks weekly internal reporting and incident triage correlation).
- No evidence of inference degradation itself; appears to be a Console data completeness/metadata issue.

Customer / context
- Company: Aurora Search
- Tier: self_serve
- Customer reports active traffic in eu-west (they are in EU business hours).

Environment
- Console: prod
- Affected area: Latency dashboard region filter + breakdown charts
- Region: eu-west

What we see internally
- Support can reproduce in their own Console account: eu-west missing from region dropdown on Latency dashboard.
- Related: we have other eu-west symptoms in Support queue (SUP-1850 embeddings timeouts) but this ticket is specifically Console visibility, not endpoint performance.

Steps to reproduce
1) Log into Console (prod)
2) Navigate to Observability > Latency
3) Open Region filter dropdown
4) Observe eu-west absent
5) Switch timeframe to 7d; still absent

Expected result
- Region dropdown includes eu-west
- Charts render data for eu-west when selected

Actual result
- eu-west not present in region filter
- Charts show other regions only

Initial triage / hypotheses
- Console region list is populated from telemetry metadata (distinct region values) rather than a static enum; if telemetry ingestion is dropping the region label, eu-west will not appear.
- Possible pipeline issue: region label normalization ("eu-west" vs "eu-west-1" vs "euw1") causing aggregation under an unexpected value that the UI intentionally hides.
- Possible UI issue: hardcoded allowlist of regions not updated for eu-west in this view (less likely, but consistent with "missing from dropdown").

Evidence collected
- Screenshot (redacted) from customer showing region dropdown missing eu-west.
- Support reproduction screenshot (internal).

Support guidance requested
- Provide an interim reporting path for eu-west latency (customer needs numbers now).
- Determine whether data is truly missing vs only missing from UI filter.

Next actions
- Observability: verify whether eu-west latency metrics exist in metrics store / dashboards.
- Console: verify region list source for the latency view and whether eu-west is filtered out.
- If data exists: fix UI/metadata to surface eu-west.
- If data missing: identify ingestion break, backfill if possible, and provide customer interim reporting instructions.

Customer-safe interim workaround (draft)
- Use the API request logs export (Console > Usage > Exports) filtered by region=eu-west to compute latency percentiles, OR
- Use the Support-provided “Support-safe quick view” dashboard link once confirmed (see ENG-4823), with eu-west preselected.

Notes / constraints
- Do not share internal dashboard links that expose other customers or non-support-safe data.
- Keep language clear that the workaround is temporary and the Console view will be corrected.
comments: 2026-02-13 09:22Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Customer report from Aurora Search: latency dashboard missing eu-west. They say they are actively serving in eu-west and need p95 latency for weekly reporting. Marking P2 since it blocks operational visibility but not an outage. Requesting Observability/Console triage to confirm if this is data pipeline vs UI allowlist.

2026-02-13 09:40Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Repro’d internally on my Support test org: eu-west not in region dropdown on Observability > Latency. Switching to other dashboards (Errors) does show eu-west, which suggests view-specific filtering or view-specific dataset.

2026-02-13 10:05Z — Allison Grant (Observability) — Acknowledged. I’ll check metrics cardinality and the dimension mapping for region in the latency dataset used by Console. Quick question: does the customer see eu-west in any other Console views (Usage, Errors, Traces)?

2026-02-13 10:12Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Customer says they see eu-west in Usage export filters but not in Latency dashboard. I can confirm I see eu-west in Usage exports (region filter) but not in Latency view.

2026-02-13 11:00Z — Allison Grant (Observability) — Initial finding: eu-west exists in raw request metrics, but the Console latency view reads from an aggregated table that is missing eu-west partitions for the last ~10 days. This looks like an ETL job config issue (region mapping) rather than the inference metrics emitter. Looping in Platform for pipeline owner.

2026-02-13 11:18Z — Ethan Park (Platform) — Thanks. We recently changed region normalization in the aggregator to map cloud regions; eu-west might be emitting as "eu-west" while the aggregator expects "eu-west-1". We’ll confirm the distinct values and patch the normalization rule. Can Observability share the exact distinct region strings present in raw vs agg?

2026-02-13 11:35Z — Allison Grant (Observability) — Raw has "eu-west"; aggregated table expects allowlisted values and currently only recognizes "eu-west-1" (which has near-zero rows). This explains why the UI dropdown never sees "eu-west" and doesn’t show it.

2026-02-13 12:10Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Interim customer guidance proposal:
1) Use Console > Usage > Exports (CSV) filtered to region=eu-west and compute p50/p95 locally (we can provide a short snippet).
2) If they can share a handful of request IDs, Support can pull latency percentiles for a defined window and send back a one-time report.
Please confirm this is OK + customer-safe.

2026-02-13 12:22Z — Allison Grant (Observability) — Approved. For self_serve, steer them to Usage export as primary workaround. If they need immediate numbers, Support can do a one-time internal pull as long as you only report their org’s data and keep the query window/timezone explicit.

2026-02-14 09:05Z — Ethan Park (Platform) — Patch in progress: update aggregator normalization to treat "eu-west" as canonical and backfill last 14 days into the aggregated latency table. ETA: patch deploy today; backfill finishes by end of day UTC barring queue delays.

2026-02-14 10:30Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Sent customer update: confirmed it’s a Console aggregation/normalization issue (not service degradation), provided interim export-based reporting steps, and set expectation that Console eu-west breakdown will return after backfill. Customer asked if historical 30d will be restored; I told them we’re targeting 14d backfill pending confirmation.

2026-02-17 16:15Z — Allison Grant (Observability) — Backfill completed for 14d. Confirmed eu-west appears in aggregated table and should be available to the Console dropdown after cache refresh. If Support still doesn’t see it, we may need a cache bust / redeploy of the Console service that serves filter options.

2026-02-18 08:50Z — Priya Shah (Support) — I now see eu-west in the Latency region dropdown on my test org. Asking customer to confirm on their side. Leaving ticket In Progress until customer confirms and we document the interim workaround as a short internal macro (so we have it if this recurs).

2026-02-18 15:40Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Follow-up: also recommending we add a lightweight pipeline check to alert Support when a region disappears from the aggregated dataset (prevents silent UI gaps). Not sure if this folds into ENG-4823 or needs separate Eng task.
